Unstressed Vowels and Vowel Reduction

There are two rules:
  1. One word has only one stress.
  2. You do not stress consonants, only vowels.
When there is more than one vowel sound in a word, the stressed vowel says its sound and the other vowels become reduced.

For example:
Banana pronounced Buh- NA- nuh. The stressed vowel (A) is pronounced clearly, and the other vowels become reduced to the sound schwa.
Take a look at some other words. Say them aloud, saying the stressed vowel clearly and the others with a reduced sound:

determined
professor
curriculum
accept
decision
Now read these sentences from the text. Remember to pronounce the vowel sounds correctly.

Expressions for Presenting Strong Opinions
When you want to express your opinions, there are many expressions you can use. It is important to be able to communicate your opinion, however strong, in a way that is clear but also polite.
Here are some expressions for presenting a strong opinion:

I'm absolutely convinced that ...
I'm sure that ...
I strongly believe that ...
I have no doubt that ...
There's no doubt in my mind that ...

For example:
There's no doubt in my mind that this book could be fantastic!

Denise: Welcome, Marisa. Thank you for coming in to see us on such short notice. Marisa, this is Kristi. She is helping out on your book.
Marisa: Nice to meet you. Thank you guys for being so generous with your time. You said in your e-mail that you had some thoughts on the book.
Denise: Indeed. Let me first say that your book is very interesting and extremely important, especially with what's going on with kids in today's technological world. We think you have a diamond in the rough here.
Marisa: But?
Denise: Marisa. We feel it's a good book, but we have determined that it could be a great book with a different ending.
Marisa: An alternative ending?

Denise: This book has a lot of potential. Let us provide you with our expertise and assistance. I'm sure that we can come to some agreement.
Marisa: Ok. What do you have in mind?
Denise: Kristi.
Kristi: Marisa. We love the story. It has a marvellous theme and is beautifully written, however the ending doesn't tie together the rest of the story. I feel that if you are able to tie the end of the story back to clues planted in the beginning, it will provide a much more positive result.
Marisa: It's not supposed to though. It is supposed to be open for interpretation. I strongly believe that kids would prefer that kind of ending to the familiar cookie-cutter style. In fact, my professor has no doubt that this is the case.

Kristi: It's always a good idea to get outside the box and try new ideas, but this book has a chance to garner a wide appeal with young readers and adults. With an alternative ending, we feel that we could sell this book to school boards and their curriculum across the country right now! Marisa, this book is very close! There's no doubt in my mind that this book could be fantastic!
Marisa: Denise, you agree with this?
Denise: We are absolutely convinced that this is the right direction to go in.
Marisa: Ok. I guess I can accept that.
Kristi: It's the right decision. Here's what we were thinking.
